newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer says will welcome new Euro currency.
newsitem.headline: Bayer says will welcome new Euro currency.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Bayer AG on Tuesday said it welcomes the planned introduction of Europe's common currency at the end of the decade and was preparing to use the Euro after 1999.
"We think the common currency Euro will be clearly positive and good for Bayer, it will also be good for Europe," Bayer chief financial officer Helmut Loehr told a news conference.

Loehr said the Bayer group was preparing for the introduction of the Euro and would be ready to adopt it in 1999. Referring to the preparations to introduce the new currency, Loehr said, "it will cost a bit of money but it will be worth it."
He did not detail the costs of a conversion.

The Euro will be adopted by nations meeting a number of strict economic and fiscal criteria on January 1, 1999. Germany and France are generally expected to be among the first nations to adopt the new currency.
